about: The feature vocabulary for the adapter protocol. An adapter's hello lists the features its implementation supports, and the runner sends only cases whose required features are all listed. Features marked composable may also appear in hello's composes list, meaning the adapter supplies that behaviour itself rather than the implementation. Names are permanent once released; a feature is retired, never renamed.

acdc.edges.description: Evaluates every edge in an ACDC's provenance DAG and reports each one it evaluated, keyed by its near node's SAID and label path. Only liveness assertions and the assertions that an edge is reported require it; an implementation without it answers incomplete for an ACDC that has edges.

acdc.keripy-1x.description: Reads the ACDC 1.x field set and computes the top-level SAID over the expanded form, as keripy 1.x does. No specification defines either; cases using it belong to the acdc-keripy-1x-interop profile.

acdc.ptel-1x.description: Verifies keripy 1.x's issuance and revocation registry (vcp, iss, rev). No specification defines it; cases using it belong to the acdc-keripy-1x-interop profile.

acdc.registry.bup.description: Verifies a blindable registry (rip and bup events, with any disclosed blinded state) and reports its verified head. Only liveness assertions and the assertions that a registry is reported require it.

acdc.version-2.x.description: Verifies ACDC 2.00 bodies, the wire the ACDC specification v1.0 defines, against a bundle of their KELs, registries, schemas and provenance. Every ACDC case requires it.

cesr.domain.binary.description: Handles the binary domain (qb2) and switches between text and binary domains within a stream.

cesr.genus-1.00.description: Reads and writes the count codes of genus AAA version 1.00, as keripy 1.x uses them. No specification defines this table; cases using it belong to the keripy-1.x interoperability profile.

cesr.genus-2.00.description: Reads and writes the count codes of genus AAA version 2.00, as defined by the CESR specification's master code table.

cesr.item-extents.description: Reports each decoded item's byte extents and group ends.

cesr.native.description: Parses message bodies encoded natively in CESR.

cesr.serialization.cbor.description: Frames and parses CBOR message bodies located by their version string.

cesr.serialization.json.description: Frames and parses JSON message bodies located by their version string.

cesr.serialization.mgpk.description: Frames and parses MessagePack message bodies located by their version string.

crypto.ed25519.description: Verifies and produces Ed25519 signatures and keys.

crypto.ed448.description: Verifies and produces Ed448 signatures and keys.

crypto.secp256k1.description: Verifies and produces ECDSA secp256k1 signatures and keys.

crypto.secp256r1.description: Verifies and produces ECDSA secp256r1 signatures and keys.

kel.basic.description: Validates inception, rotation and interaction events for a single-signature transferable identifier.

kel.delegation.description: Validates delegated inception and rotation against the delegator's anchoring seal.

kel.multisig.numeric.description: Validates numeric signing and next thresholds over several keys.

kel.multisig.weighted.description: Validates fractionally weighted signing and next thresholds, including multiple clauses.

kel.partial-rotation.description: Validates partial and reserve rotation, including dual-indexed signatures.

kel.recovery.description: Accepts a rotation that the superseding rules permit, and keeps the events it displaces as seen but off the trunk. Only the assertions that such a rotation is accepted require this feature; refusing a rotation the rules do not permit is required of every validator, so cases that check it never require it.

kel.witness.description: Validates witness receipts and witness thresholds, including witness rotation.

keri.duplicity.description: Records a conflicting event as duplicitous rather than only declining it.

keri.escrow.description: Holds events that are valid but not yet acceptable, and accepts them when what they wait for arrives. Only the assertions that a held event is later accepted require this feature; that such an event is not accepted on arrival is required of every validator, so cases that check it never require it.

keri.routing.description: Routes each incoming message to the processing it needs (key event, receipt, reply) and drives the implementation to quiescence after each delivery.

keri.version-1.x.description: Accepts KERI message bodies carrying the legacy 1.XX version string.

keri.version-2.x.description: Accepts KERI message bodies carrying the 2.XX version string.
